messages:
Maya: quick q — for the prefix-cache key namespace, should we do tenant-level or tenant+route+model? trying to avoid broad invalidations. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/1234
Sam: tenant+route+model. same prompt text can be used by different routes with different post-processing. trades off keyspace for correctness.
Jordan: include model variant (eg gpt-small-q8 vs gpt-small-fp16) — outputs can differ. also include model version.
Anya: agree, include model_id + version. also auth scope (shared/private) matters for collisions.
Maya: ok so namespace = tenant_id | route | model_id | model_version | auth_scope. quick Q on TTL: default to 24h? can client `Cache-Control:max-age` raise it?
Sam: server-side TTL should be authoritative. allow client to request a lower max-age but never longer than server derived TTL. server TTL can be based on prompt determinism heuristics.
Maya: streaming clients — how do we signal a cache hit? header isn't enough for SSE/streaming.
Sam: non-streaming: `x-prefix-cache: hit` header (and `x-prefix-cache-ttl`). streaming: emit an initial event chunk indicating hit, e.g. `data: {"type":"cache_hit","ttl":86400}` as the first data frame, then close stream with cached payload. keep both for backcompat.
Jordan: older clients expect a boolean in the JSON response body e.g. { "cache_hit": true }. we should keep that for non-streaming. for streaming, add an initial JSON chunk { "cache_hit": true } before the content.
OpsBot: deploy canary scheduled: staging at 12:30 UTC, prod canary at 13:10 UTC if checks pass :rocket:
Anya: about invalidation — proposal: tombstone approach with per-namespace incremental `invalidation_version`. write tombstone for prefix-id; cache key lookup includes current invalidation_version. simple to check and O(1) invalidation.
Sam: sounds good. note on prefix normalization: we must canonicalize prefixes (lowercase, collapse whitespace, strip punctuation?) and then hash. clients need explicit rules.
Maya: let's be explicit: normalization = unicode normalize (NFKC), lowercase, collapse internal whitespace to single space, trim ends. do not strip punctuation (some punctuation matters). hash with sha256 and use first 128 bits. document it.
Jordan: tests: unit test for normalization, integration test for streaming hit chunk, compatibility test for legacy JSON boolean and header. perf test to check namespace cardinality. I'll review PR today.
Sam: I'll add spec doc in docs repo and SDK note (client side normalizer helpers).
Anya: feature flag request: add `prefix_cache_streaming_hit` so we can gate streaming hit behavior during rollout.
Maya: added flag `prefix_cache_streaming_hit` in config and the PR description. also added `x-prefix-cache-ttl` header plan. @Jordan @Sam please ack.
Jordan: acked. small nit: prefer header name `x-prefix-cache: hit|miss` rather than `x-prefix-cache-hit: true`. one header to convey state is simpler.
Sam: agree. also include `x-prefix-cache-ttl` (seconds) for observability.
Maya: example header for non-streaming responses:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-prefix-cache: hit
x-prefix-cache-ttl: 86400
content-type: application/json
```
Maya: and streaming example (SSE initial chunk):
```
data: {"type":"cache_hit","ttl":86400}

data: {"type":"cached_payload","payload":{...}}
```
Anya: one more: invalidation API path — should it be `/v1/namespaces/{ns}/invalidate` with body {"prefix_hash": "...","version": 42}?
Sam: yes that works. require authenticated admin token and emit audit log.
Maya: I'll update the PR with the namespace composition, normalization spec, header names, streaming chunk example, invalidation API and test plan. tagging reviewers. thanks all :heart:
Sam: ping me once PR is updated, I'll run the perf job.
Jordan: taking code review this afternoon. will comment on edgecases.
OpsBot: canary complete on staging, smoke passed.
Maya: closing loop — will merge behind feature flag after fixes and tests.
